title: Experiment signal fabric and eval-gating integration
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Objective: Create a unified 'signal fabric' and integrate it with our experiment gating service so that A/B tests, canaries and progressive rollouts use consistent, normalized metrics and automatic gating decisions. The fabric will centralize metric transforms (percentiles, p95/p99, delta-from-baseline), outlier detection, and normalization across cohorts to reduce false positives and noisy rollbacks.

Scope:
- Define canonical signal set for core surface area (latency, error-rate, model-quality regressions using eval prompts).
- Implement a lightweight signal adapter library that normalizes and tags events before they reach the gating service.
- Wire gating rules to the existing rollout engine (canary/gradual-release) so gates are evaluated automatically and can initiate stage hold/rollback.
- Add dashboards and tracing hooks for SRE/PM visibility and postmortem analysis.

Success criteria:
- Consistent signal transformation used by >=3 experiment types (A/B, canary, reranking) across at least two services within 4 weeks.
- Fewer false-positive rollbacks: reduce noise-triggered rollbacks by 40% on pilot experiments.
- Automated gate decision latency < 60s for streaming signals during a 1% traffic canary.

Instrumentation & metrics:
- Canonical metrics: request_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), token_error_rate, eval_regression_score (delta vs baseline).
- Normalization: cohort bucketing rules (country, model_variant, sequence_length_group).
- Statistical tests: two-sided bootstrap for model-quality signals, sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) for latency/error signals.
- Observability: per-gate signal health panel (Grafana), gate-decision event log (Kafka topic: experiments.gate.decisions), and trace links to PRs and rollout metadata.

Gating policy prototype:
- Soft gate at 1%: monitor for 1 hour; if any high-confidence model-quality regression > 3% and corroborated by at least two eval prompts, mark as HOLD and notify.
- Hard gate at 10%: require no high-confidence regressions for 24 hours and p95 latency within 12% of baseline.
- Auto-rollback: if hard gate fails with high-confidence regression OR error-rate spike > 2x baseline sustained for 15m, trigger rollback to previous model variant and page on-call.

Rollout plan (pilot):
1) Week 0 (design+spec): finalize canonical signals and wireframe dashboards. Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EX/pages/Signal+Fabric+Spec (draft).
2) Week 1 (build): adapter library + gating API shim; small landing PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/experiments/pull/449, /pull/452.
3) Week 2 (pilot): run against two internal experiments (search-relevance A/B and hosted-api canary).
4) Week 3 (iterate): tune thresholds, add metric smoothing.
5) Week 4 (ramp): enable for broader experiments and bake into release controls.

Trade-offs considered:
- Centralizing transforms reduces divergence but introduces a single source of failure; mitigation: adapter runs client-side with circuit breaker and degraded-mode passthrough.
- Stronger statistical tests increase compute; mitigation: run heavy tests on sampled windows and use lightweight SPRT for streaming.

Reviews & feedback:
- SRE (Kiran Patel): requested explicit backpressure rules for gate-eval ingestion and explained existing quota shapes (see ENG-61204).
- Applied ML (Dr. Mei Wong): recommended adding synthetic prompts for early detection of quality regressions and suggested bootstrap thresholds.
- Legal/Comms: suggested careful customer messaging for auto-rollbacks affecting production traffic.

Open risks / blockers:
- Need kernel-level latency telemetry from serving runtime (ENG-4820) to compute true p95 under load.
- Dashboards require expanded retention on the experiments metrics stream (cost request to infra).

Follow-ups / next steps:
- Eng to deliver ingestion adapter (owner: ENG-61204), SLO/latency telemetry (owner: ENG-4820).
- PM to finalize gating policy doc and acceptance matrix; schedule cross-functional signoff (SRE, ML, Legal).
- Create a small-run pilot with two internal teams; collect 2 weeks of signal history, then re-evaluate thresholds.

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence spec (draft): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EX/pages/Signal+Fabric+Spec
- Pilot PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/experiments/pull/449, https://github.com/redwood-inference/experiments/pull/452
- Pilot dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/exp/signal-fabric-pilot

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Adapter library merged and published, gating API accepts canonical signals, pilot experiments exercised gates per policy and SRE runbook created for rollback & incident response.

Notes: Avoid coupling to any single telemetry vendor; adapter must be configurable for multiple backends (Prometheus, Datadog, internal metrics bus). Keep gating decisions auditable: every gate decision must have a persisted event with input signals, threshold values, and model/version metadata.
